Messages.Author: Tim Eijpe
Messages.Body:
Now this came up in the "if you think that..." thread.
Augustus does not seem to have inherent stealth on his retreaval action.
However wouldn't that be moot anyway? It is an action taken by a vampire the
controlling methuselah's ready region not directing prey or predator.
Wouldn't
it therefore be a +1 stealth action per definition? It would IMO go along
the
same lines as a Graverobbing from my own torpor region, which would be at +1
Stealth.
Would you please clarify this to me?

Cardtext:
Augustus Giovanni: 11/11
-AUS DOM NEC POT cel pre
-Augustus has 2 votes. If a vampire you control has been burned since
your
last turn, Augustus may move that vampire from your ash heap to the
ready region as an action that costs 1 pool. +1 bleed

Thanks,
Tim Eijpe

Messages.Author: Andy Brown
Messages.Body:


I would say not, as he is performing a non-directed action, to retrieve
a card from your ash heap. This is not the same as entering your own
torpor
region, as it is not in the minion play area.

Just my own opinion of the wording, LSJ would probably have to confirm,
or
we could be arguing till the Antediluvians awake.

Andy

Messages.Author: Halcyan 2
Messages.Body:
>>I meant that actions taken in your own ready region are at +1 stealth per
>>default, right? That is what I meant with definition.
>
>No.
>
>What definition are you pointing to? This is not in the rules book, or
>any of the online rulings.

I was a little surprised by Tim's assertions as well.

Perhaps he got the impression that since actions to rescue oneself from torpor
are at +1 stealth, actions to rescue other vampires in your own region are +1
stealth (but not when directed at others), and actions to diablerize your own
vampires are at +1 stealth (but not diablerie of others' vampires), he got the
incorrect impression that *all* actions concerning one's own torpor region get
+1 stealth.

Halcyan 2
